title: Computing the Random 3-SAT Threshold
main_claim: The uniform random 3-SAT threshold alpha_3 exists (strict-side limits of p(n, floor(an))). It is a computable real: one fixed Turing machine outputs a 2^-r approximation on input 1^r. Lower certificates come from f_n/n - 2^67 n^{-1/6} <= alpha. Upper certificates are rational finite site-only hierarchical trials with G_1(a,beta;Q) < 0, which are sound because P <= G_1 and complete because P = inf G_1.
coverage:
I read the whole LaTeX source: introduction, certificates, proof-map, probability, trials, sensitivity, transition, closure and assembly.

Checked line by line, including constants:
- Free-deletion moment lemma: the incident-killing bound (q+60/n)^2, the 2-to-3-literal replacement loss 16/(27d^2), the bin parameters, the Chebyshev step, the delay-integral identity, and the per-bin bound 2^47 (j+1)^2 2^{-j/5}. Numerically I checked the sums 1710 < 2^11, the small-q term 2^17.3 < 2^18, and e*Gamma(1/5)*4^{1/5} < 2^7.
- Martingale p-moment concentration (C_1 = 2^62).
- Weighted interpolation lemma: the convexity step, and the Fourier/complement-invariance proof that equalizing variable weights cannot lower the satisfiability probability.
- Almost-superadditivity and the dyadic merging, giving 2^67 k^{-1/6} with D_b ~ 8.17.
- Threshold bounds [1/200, 10] by first moment and Hall's theorem; transfer from the relaxed Poisson model to proper clauses by thinning.
- Computability of f_n by truncated Poisson sums.
- Robustness above threshold (linear deletion, C_4 = 2^53) and the signs of the soft pressure.
- Superadditivity of the pressure.
- Soundness interpolation for site-only trials: the derivative sign and the identity x^3 + 2y^3 - 3xy^2 = (x-y)^2(x+2y), checked with sympy.
- Reservoir rate algebra (mu_{>=2}, Delta_A, Delta_B, total 12M+6k).
- Depth-independent exponent-sensitivity lemma (variance budget 5C^2, the density bound by summation by parts).
- Lemma 2.1, the certificate search, and the assembly.

Checked at the argument level only (logic and hypotheses, not every estimate):
- Completeness machinery: the Gaussian Ghirlanda-Guerra probing lemma (convexity, integration by parts, the uniformity claims); the Dovbysh-Sudakov / Panchenko sphere and ultrametricity bridge; the componentwise ordering of the vector overlaps; the two-cut quantile band; the RPC partition prediction (n_C - x)/n and the independence of the decorations from the partition; the Austin-Panchenko product-tree representation; endpoint passage with new exponents m*x_1, m*x_2, m, t_2..t_d; preservation of old records and construction of the new record via the Hilbert-space support-diameter lemma; termination by geometric decrease of the first exponent.
- Closure: kernel collapse with Lipschitz/Wasserstein propagation (bound R), the small-exponent replacement, the order in which the epsilons are chosen, and the rational discretization.

I found no step that fails. The deepest and least independently verifiable part is the completeness argument (transition plus closure), which claims to remove shared nonroot coordinates in a diluted 3-SAT model. That goes past the published Panchenko results. I checked its logic and hypotheses but could not verify every estimate exhaustively.
sibling_notes: The board key hive:oai_math:review:fam:235 was empty when I started, so there were no sibling findings to use. The paper cites companions (FixedClauseThreshold, OpenAIDilutedPressure2026), but neither is needed in the proof chain: it proves existence of the threshold itself, and cites the companions only to identify constants and for context, so the argument is not circular. I posted my verdict to the board.
